description:
FILED s492c (Opus, 2026-09-21), as #2007's "measure first" half.

#2007 asked whether the real (pure-Perl) File::Spec::Unix could replace the
shim, judged by PathTools' own t/Spec.t.  It could not be measured here:

  * `Pl::Parser`'s inc_paths BEGINS with PCL's shim lib/ (and the runtime's
    %p-shim-lib-dir-p says so in as many words), so a `use lib` pointing at
    perl's own lib cannot shadow `lib/File/Spec.pm` -- the shim wins, and the
    real module never loads even when it is on the path.
  * Running PathTools' t/Spec.t in the dist directory does not help either:
    `-Ilib` there puts the DIST's own `lib/Cwd.pm` (the XS one) first, so the
    file dies "Can't locate Cwd.pm in @INC (the module is XS...)" before it
    reaches File::Spec at all.  That is the row the s492c modtests BEFORE
    table shows (PathTools 76 of 823).

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT NEEDS: a way to ask for a specific module file
regardless of the shim -- either an env switch that drops the shim dir from
inc_paths for one run, or copying the real File/Spec*.pm into a directory and
transpiling them by path rather than by module name.  Either is ten minutes;
neither existed, and inventing one inside a correctness batch was the wrong
trade.

Meanwhile #2007 fixed the shim function by function against the real
File::Spec::Unix's source (catdir, catfile, abs2rel, case_tolerant), which is
the task's own fallback.
subject: The `replace lib/File/Spec.pm with the real File::Spec::Unix` measurement cannot be taken: PCL`s shim lib/ wins module RESOLUTION over any `use lib`, so the real module cannot be loaded to compare
